verdict.rationale: Slate's own docs describe spinning up multiple background subagents, shown as a grid of cards, to parallelize work across several tasks while you keep talking to Slate. They also describe multi-hour sessions, and a --yolo flag removes approval prompts so agents can run unattended. Missing for 10: any evidence of runs lasting days, documented fleet scale or concurrency limits, and independent or hands-on confirmation that long parallel runs work.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can launch fleets of autonomous agents that work in parallel on different tasks for hours or days

citations.quote: While one or more agents run in the background, you can keep talking with Slate: plan next steps, queue up additional tasks, or spin up more agents to parallelize work across several tasks at once.
Those agents show up as a grid of inline subagent cards, one per agent.
Slate works with you across long, multi-hour sessions.
We support `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (alias: `--yolo`) to bypass permission prompts.
